answer.rationale:
Constraints eliminate the strongest-looking precedent first: memory_b1 (rollback cleared a checkout error spike) is unusable because compliance has ruled the security patch must not be reverted, so rollback_release is off the table regardless of its track record. The remaining tension is between memory_b2 (regional failover recovered latency in minutes, and today's degradation is conveniently confined to the primary region) and memory_b5 (routing report/read queries off the primary restored write latency same-day). Failover pattern-matches the symptom geography, but it is the one option that directly endangers the hard constraint: shifting regions during peak settlement with heavy writes puts in-flight and replicating writes at risk, and the primary objective is sustained availability WITHOUT losing customer writes. memory_b2's record says 'traffic shifted cleanly' during a March degradation but I do not know whether that was a write-heavy peak or a low-write window 	he archive pull is meant to settle; if March was a light-write period, the memory does not license failover now. I therefore intend route_read_replicas: it is load-shedding on the contended primary, reversible, and does not move the write path at all, so a wrong call degrades a dashboard rather than dropping a settlement. I am verifying memory_b5 to check whether the day-55 recovery was actually causally attributable to replica routing or merely coincident with the load dropping on its own, and memory_b2 to see the write profile and any data-loss caveats behind 'shifted cleanly'. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: I have no evidence the current climb shares a cause with day 55 ead amplification vs. a genuine regression in the 2-hour-old release, which I cannot revert), and the 90-minute climb starting after the release is suspicious. If replica routing does not bend the p99 curve within roughly 20-30 minutes, the release-regression hypothesis strengthens and enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4, fail-fast to protect the rest of the checkout path) becomes the next candidate rather than failover. A standing bias worth flagging: this memory set records only interventions that worked, so it overstates how reliably any of these tactics generalize
